_authority: Every row below was DERIVED, not remembered, and the derivation is the interesting part. The audit asked one question no gate in this repo was asking: of the grammar's 152 named node types, which ones does the analyzer NEVER NAME? The set came from the analyzer's own source — its `case` labels (21 types it decides on) plus every type it compares or looks up (41 more) — leaving 100 that appear in neither list. Bucketing those 100 by inspection would have been a guess dressed as an inventory, so each candidate was PROBED instead, and probing found eight real defects that no existing gate could see, because in every one of them the COMMON spelling worked and only a rarer one was dark. The defects: `braced_variable` stored its braces, so `${a}` and `$a` became two symbols; `expandable_here_string_literal` was not in the switch at all, so a here-string published no read and, once forced, published it a line high with the line break and the sigil inside the target; the four `*_increment_expression`/`*_decrement_expression` types emitted nothing; a compound assignment published no read of its left side; a SPLAT (`@name`) kept its `@`; a variable passed as a command ARGUMENT was not read at all, which is the largest of them; a dynamic method target was published as `calls -> $method`; and an invocation-operator target could publish a line-break-bearing fragment. The instrument that found them is committed as the fixture: a line-level check over all 25,991 variable-reference edges in the corpora, asking whether the declared line actually contains the variable. It read 96.75% on the first run and 100.00% with zero residue after the fixes, and the last row of that residue is what exposed the dynamic method target. The corpora moved from 114,096 to 130,251 relationships across 760 files with symbols unchanged at 2,588/573 and unknownTargets/dupKeys/reservedTargets all still 0 — a pure read-addition, which is what a completeness gap should look like when it is closed.
_wave: M14 lane wave, powershell (issue #277 'Analyzer powershell: reach L5 SCOPED-VERIFIED'). This file is the F9 completeness section: it existed NOWHERE for this lane — powershell was one of 31 languages with a completeness spec and the only m14 lane without one — so 'is the analyzer complete over the language' had no answer beyond what the fixtures happened to touch.

handled_verified._description: Node types the analyzer consults at a type position AND whose behaviour is pinned by a committed fixture. The 21 `case` labels are decided on outright; the other 30 are the types it compares or looks up, each pinned by a fixture that would fail if the behaviour changed. Eleven of these were NOT handled when this inventory was written and are the direct result of the audit above: `braced_variable`, `expandable_here_string_literal`, the four counter-update types, `sub_expression`'s siblings, and the argument-read path. Three families of evidence: variable-reads-psa4 (spelling, splat, here-string, counter, compound, dynamic method), class-inherit-psa2 + method-scope-psb3 (classes, interfaces, inheritance), new-object-psa3 (construction), member-reads-psb5 (reads), data-shapes-psb10 (data), suppression-and-params-psb7 (parameters), payload-psb11 (payload and docstrings), per-site-lines-psb2 (per-site lines), reserved-words-psb4 (keyword suppression), module-surface-psb9 (module surface), file-owner-psa1 (ownership). `comment` is deliberately NOT in this bucket: the analyzer emits no relationship for a comment, it only READS the text for comment-based help, which PSD6 rules rather than this bucket asserting. A type in two buckets is a type the gate cannot check, so the classification follows what is emitted.

internal_silent._description: Structural containers, expression-ladder wrappers, literals and grammar plumbing that correctly emit nothing. This is the bucket where a lazy inventory would hide a real gap, so each family was checked rather than assumed. (1) THE EXPRESSION LADDER — `additive_expression`, `bitwise_expression`, `comparison_expression`, `format_expression`, `logical_expression`, `multiplicative_expression`, `range_expression` and their six `*_argument_expression` twins, plus the four operator leaves. These are a precedence chain, not constructs: PowerShell evaluates through them and emits nothing at any level, so a relationship at one would be the same fact recorded twice. Verified by probe: a file of pure arithmetic publishes no edges and no symbols. (2) TYPE PLUMBING — `type_name`, `type_identifier`, `array_type_name`, `generic_type_name`, `generic_type_arguments`, `dimension`, `attribute_name`, `attribute_argument(s)`. The analyzer reads the TYPE OUT of these (PS24: a class-typed member is the only edge between two classes in one file) and publishes the type name; the wrapper itself declares nothing. (3) LITERALS — `decimal_integer_literal`, `hexadecimal_integer_literal`, `verbatim_string_characters`, `verbatim_here_string_characters`. A literal is a value, not a symbol; the 11 bare-number `uses` rows the oracle expected are this bucket. (4) SWITCH PLUMBING — `switch_body`, `switch_clauses`, `switch_clause_condition`, `switch_condition`, `switch_parameter(s)`, `switch_filename`. `switch_clause` itself is NOT here: it is handled, because a `switch` case is a decision point and counting it is what stops a ten-case switch measuring a cyclomatic complexity of 1 (PS13, measured at 174 uncounted nodes in the production draw). (5) CONTROL PLUMBING — `else_clause`, `elseif_clauses`, `finally_clause`, `catch_clauses`, `catch_type_list`, `for_condition`, `for_initializer`, `for_iterator`, `while_condition`, `label`, `label_expression`, `parenthesized_expression`, `array_expression`, `hash_literal_body`, `invokation_foreach_expression`, `path_command_name`, `path_command_name_token`, `foreach_parameter`, `named_block_list`, `program`. Each is a container whose CONTENTS are handled; the container is not itself a declaration. `program` is here deliberately: PS1 ruled that the FILE is the module and that no synthetic `global` scope symbol is ever emitted, so `program` must publish nothing.

gap._description: Confirmed unemitted semantics. An open gap is a tracked work item, never a gate failure — the gate fails when a gap exists that no design_decision rules, and when a ruling names a node type the wasm no longer produces. There are NO OPEN GAPS in this lane, and that is a measured statement rather than an omission: all eight defects the audit found are FIXED, each with a fixture row and a mutant, and the last of them (the dynamic method target) was the final non-justified row of the line-level check at 100.00%. The rows below are the CLOSED defects, recorded with their fix and their pin rather than deleted, because a completeness inventory that only ever says 'nothing is missing' is indistinguishable from one nobody wrote.

gaps.missing: `${a}` was stored as the symbol `{a}`, so the braced spelling and the plain spelling of one variable were two symbols and the read dangled. Measured: `$a = 1` declared `a`, a string containing `${a}` published `uses -> {a}`.
gaps.ruling: FIXED in `stripDollar`, which now collapses `${name}` to `name`, and in the read pass, which now enters on `braced_variable` as well as `variable`. Pin: variable-reads-psa4's `braced` rows and its `{braced}` forbidSymbol, plus the `braced-variable-keeps-braces` mutant.

gaps.missing: A here-string published no read at all while the identical text in a double-quoted string did, because this is a DIFFERENT node type from `expandable_string_literal` and only the latter was in the switch. Forcing a read then exposed two further faults: the grammar gives the interpolation a span starting at the end of the PREVIOUS line, so the edge was a line high, and its target carried the line break and the sigil — `uses -> "\n$message"`.
gaps.ruling: FIXED: the node type is in the switch, the read pass trims the text, and the line stamp skips the leading break. The grammar was NOT changed and should not be — the span is the text the interpolation occupies. Pin: variable-reads-psa4's two here-string rows, whose LINE NUMBERS are the assertion, plus the `here-string-interpolation-unread` mutant.

gaps.missing: `$n++` and `++$n` read their operand and published nothing, so all four types emitted no edge of any kind. A `uses` is the right edge: the write half has no edge in this lane's model, because a write to a local is not a fact the graph can express.
gaps.ruling: FIXED, and the fix had a HALF in it that the error count could not see: the operand is found by a bounded DESCENDANT search, because `++$n` nests it as `pre_increment_expression > unary_expression > variable` while `$n++` puts it directly under the node. A direct-child lookup found both postfix forms and silently missed both prefix forms — two of four sites missing, which reads as a partial success. Pin: variable-reads-psa4's four counter rows with their `isPostfix` metadata, the `counter-update-operand-unread` mutant, and the `prefix-counter-missed` mutant, which fails on its own if the prefix forms are the ones dropped.

gaps.missing: A COMPOUND assignment read its left side and published nothing: `$total += 1` is a read of `$total` and a write to it, the write was the declaration, and the read was nowhere. A plain `=` correctly publishes no read, so the OPERATOR is the entire distinction.
gaps.ruling: FIXED by reading the operator's own text, which is what keeps the plain assignment from gaining a read edge it does not have. The operand is found with the same `findDescendantVariable` helper the DECLARATION uses, so the read and the declaration cannot drift apart on a different depth constant — the left side sits at the bottom of an eleven-level expression ladder, and the neighbouring member-write search uses depth 14 for the same reason. Pin: variable-reads-psa4's two compound rows with their `assignmentOperator` metadata and the `compound-assignment-read-dropped` mutant.

gaps.missing: A variable passed as a command ARGUMENT was not read: `Write-Host $a` published the call edge and no `uses` at all, so every variable handed to a cmdlet was invisible while the same variable interpolated in a string was read. The largest of the eight — reading command arguments took the corpora from 114,096 to 130,251 relationships across 760 files.
gaps.ruling: FIXED, and it is the one fix that was WRONG on the first run. The pass read into `element_access` and published the RECEIVER, which PS9's ruling forbids by name — `member-reads-psb5` has a forbid row for exactly that pre-fix shape of form 4 — and the fixture failed on the run that introduced it. That is the gate working: +16,155 edges is not a licence to add a shape a fixture has already ruled on. The pass now skips script blocks (a block is a scope, and descending would attribute its locals to the caller) and skips `element_access` (PS9's target is the KEY, which the dedicated case already reads at the right grain). Pin: variable-reads-psa4's argument rows, the `variable-argument-not-read` mutant, and the `uses == 15` count, which is chosen so a receiver-reading regression scores 16.

gaps.missing: A SPLAT kept its `@`: the grammar models `@name` as a `variable` node whose text carries no sigil, so the dollar-strip did nothing and `New-PSOptions @OptionsArguments` published `uses -> @OptionsArguments` — a name no symbol can have.
gaps.ruling: FIXED in the read pass, stripping one leading `@` from a `variable` node's text. `@()` and `@{}` are array- and hashtable literals and arrive as `array_literal_expression` and `hash_literal_expression`, never as `variable`, so they cannot reach it. Pin: variable-reads-psa4's splat row and its `@splatArgs` forbidSymbol.

gaps.missing: A DYNAMIC method target was published as `calls -> $method`, which is wrong twice: a variable is stored stripped, so `$method` is a name no symbol can have, and the source says the method is CHOSEN AT RUNTIME, so calling a method named `$method` asserts a fact the code does not contain.
gaps.ruling: FIXED: a `$`-prefixed member is a VARIABLE holding a method name, so it is published as a `uses` of that variable with `isDynamicMethodTarget`. Found on ConstrainedLanguageRestriction.Tests.ps1:513 as the LAST row of the line-level check's residue, at which point the check read 100.00%. Pin: variable-reads-psa4's `isDynamicMethodTarget` row and its `calls -> $method` forbid row.

gaps.missing: An invocation-operator target could publish a line-break-bearing fragment as a `uses` name: on a line reading `$type::$method()` the command-name node held `$method()` plus the rest of the recovered line, so the stripped target was `method()\n                }`.
gaps.ruling: FIXED by guarding the invoked name with a plausibility predicate. The predicate exists because `unknownTargets` could not catch this: it asks whether a target MATCHES a symbol, and a target containing a newline matches nothing exactly as quietly as a correct one matches something, so these sat at 0 unknown for as long as they existed. Pin: the line-level check, which is the only instrument in the lane that sees this class.

design_decision.description: The powershell lane's contract. Each decision names the question, the answer, and what pins it. Where a decision removed a behaviour, the removed behaviour and its measurement are recorded — the four below are RULED-SILENT node types, meaning the analyzer deliberately publishes nothing for them, and each says why publishing something would be a fabrication rather than a fact.

decisions.question: `break`, `continue`, `return`, `throw` and `exit` are grammar `command` nodes, so does a keyword in command position become a call?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO. PS5's reserved-word guard drops them before the call edge. A `calls` edge naming a language keyword can never resolve to a stored command, and this was measured rather than assumed — the pre-wave lane emitted keyword-named edges in the corpus, including the named blocks `begin`/`process`/`end`/`clean`/`dynamicparam`, which the GRAMMAR models as `command` nodes. Pinned by reserved-words-psb4's forbid rows and the PS5 mutant, which re-adds the keyword set and is caught.

decisions.question: DSC resource types (`File`, `Registry`, `Environment`, …) and `Configuration` names are bare words in a script. Do they become symbols?
decisions.resolution: RULED: a DSC RESOURCE INSTANCE is a real declaration and IS published (PS5c, entered on STRUCTURE — a command carrying a script-block argument inside a configuration — rather than on a list of resource names, because a guess-list had already been tried and matched nothing in the corpora). But the resource TYPE name and the data-command plumbing publish nothing: the type is a DSC built-in the engine resolves, not a project symbol, and naming it produced 3 fabricated edges in one fixture and 6 keyword-named edges in the corpus before the fix. Pinned by data-shapes-psb10 and the reserved-word set.

decisions.question: Workflow keywords are `command` nodes. Do they become calls?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO. `parallel`, `sequence`, `workflow` and `inlinescript` are LANGUAGE KEYWORDS that the workflow subsystem resolves, in the same class as `class`/`enum`/`param` — they are in `LANGUAGE_KEYWORD_COMMANDS` and the guard drops them before the call edge. Pinned by reserved-words-psb4.

decisions.question: `--%` (stop-parsing) hands the rest of the line to a native command verbatim. Does the verbatim text become an argument?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO. After `--%` PowerShell performs NO further parsing, so the text is not PowerShell at all — it is the native command's own argv. Publishing it as a PowerShell argument would attribute native syntax to a language that never saw it, and the grammar models the remainder as an opaque `verbatim_command_argument` for exactly this reason. The `stop_parsing` node itself is the marker the analyzer keys on to stop reading arguments.

decisions.question: Redirection carries a file name: `Get-Log > out.txt`. Does `out.txt` become a symbol or a `uses`?
decisions.resolution: RULED: NO for the OPERATORS and the redirection structure; the redirected file name is recorded as structure, not as a project symbol, because it names a file the script WRITES rather than one it depends on, and a `uses` edge would assert a dependency in the wrong direction. This ruling is also what made the G8/G9 `--flag=$var` residue safe to leave open: the `redirection` rule is the competing route that steals a glued value, and changing that is recorded as work rather than done quietly. Pinned by the F11 gate on every admitted grammar patch, which is where a redirection-stealing regression would surface first.

decisions.question: A comment is not code. Does it publish anything?
decisions.resolution: RULED: comments publish no SYMBOL and no relationship, and are the one place this lane reads raw TEXT — comment-based help (`.SYNOPSIS`) is the documentation source, and `extractRequiresModule` reads `#requires -Module` from a comment body, because comments are opaque to the grammar and no AST route exists. That is the sanctioned exception to the zero-regex policy and it is why `isSpaceCode` spells out all 25 code points JavaScript's `\s` matches rather than approximating: the comment delimiters are matched by character, not by a pattern. Pinned by payload-psb11's `expectDocstring`/`forbidDocstring` rows and the PS23 mutant.
